result.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could only refute the stated failure MECHANISM, not the defect. The premise is real and I reproduced it two independent ways; one named consequence is false; the IDEMPOTENT_OPS half of the finding is real in mechanism but immaterial in magnitude.

CONFIRMED (core claim). guidance/B01.yaml:94 declares `root: cs_winsor(_) -> operand` as `action: rewrite`, and partura/steer.py:270 `canonical()` feeds BOTH `dedup_key()` (:283) and `explain()/weight()/banned()` (:294). All 15 of the project's own corpus pairs (v_base vs win) collapse to one dedup_key. The rule is NOT an identity: on a synthetic panel scored through the project's own cs_winsor kernel and partura/books.py, root cs_winsor is an EXACT no-op for the top-decile book at hl=0 (book overlap 1.000, d long_sharpe exactly 0.000) and a genuinely different book at hl>=1 (overlap 0.84 at hl=1 falling to 0.54 at hl=20). Every corpus pair ran at hl>=1 and 13 of 15 at hl>=5, so the identity never actually applies in practice. The reporter's stated mechanism for WHY (daily re-estimated clip + the reward's causal EMA mixing days, so ema(clip(x)) is not a monotone map of ema(x)) is exactly right, and the hl=0 boundary is exactly where it breaks.

The magnitude is real and the finding's F112 numbers are exact (I read them straight out of runs/F112_scale_spow_masktop/sweep_s3.json): v_base utrain long_sharpe 0.7389 / train long_ann +0.0366 / valid +0.0535 vs win -0.2462 / -0.0208 / +0.0118, both at hl_long_u 20 and sign -1, corr_orig 0.826. Over the full 15-factor corpus: median d = +0.003, median |d| = 0.025, but 2 of 15 sit outside the project's own declared noise band (evidence_base.noise_band_sharpe = 0.3) and BOTH flip the sign of train long_ann — F112 (-0.985) and F110_ret_fair_log (+0.31, base utrain -0.03 -> win +0.28). min corr_orig over the 15 is 0.566 (F106), not the 0.99 the rule's `why` quotes (0.99 is the median, 0.994). Note the project's own evidence table already records this: research/alpha_distillation/B01_reverse_guidance.md:57 gives `win` as 7% clearly better / 7% clearly worse of 15 — i.e. 1 up and 1 down outside the band — while the rule's `why` reports only the median.

REFUTED (the stated consequence). "in scripts/idea_search.py:222 whichever spelling is proposed first wins and the other returns False as equivalent -> the reported number for one is attributed to the other" is false. I replayed that exact gate: the survivor is accepted unchanged and scored by ParturaScorer on ITS OWN panel, and the reported expression is the archive CSV's own `expression` column (idea_search.py:284), so no number is ever pinned on the wrong expression. The only Partura hooks installed in AlphaCube are make_scorer, _pick and acceptable — nothing replaces the tree with its canonical form before scoring. What actually happens is a silent, RNG-dependent loss: one of two materially different experiments is never evaluated, and which one survives depends on proposal order. Scope check: `Guidance` is imported only by scripts/idea_search.py, so the recorded numbers in runs/ are uncorrupted — the blast radius is a steered search only.

The reporter also missed the one path where the written and the evaluated expression really do diverge: idea_search.py:244 canonicalizes SEEDS (`parse(G.canonical(s), ...)`), so a seed written with a root cs_winsor is planted without it (verified). That collides with the guidance's own idea I4_intraday_reversal_tail, whose grammar nominates `cs_winsor(_)` as a convex op to explore (B01.yaml:156) and therefore gets an 8x IDEA_OPS sampling boost — the guidance boosts and rewrites away the same operator. And because weight()/banned() run on the canonical form, `cs_winsor(cross_zscore(day_std(Amt), 20))` inherits B1's ban (weight 0.000, verified) even though clipping the cross-section is precisely the remedy for B1's "peak detector" complaint. These are `rewrite`-vs-`weight` consequences the finding does not mention and are the stronger part of the case.

REFUTED (IDEMPOTENT_OPS half). The mechanism is right but it does not change numbers. cs_winsor is not exactly idempotent (nanquantile's linear interpolation moves the clip point: relative 6.3e-3, 2.0% of cells move on heavy-tailed input), yet the book consequence is d long_sharpe +0.0175 at hl=20 on 36 of 72000 book cells — about 6% of the declared 0.3 noise band, and exactly 0 at hl=0. cs_robust_z is exactly rank-preserving within a day (verified), so it is an exact no-op at hl=0; even in the worst case I could construct (a count/share panel with MAD == 0 exactly, where panel values differ by a factor of 1e9 between rz(x) and rz(rz(x))) the book difference at hl=20 is d long_sharpe +0.0051 on 32 of 30000 cells. So collapsing f(f(x)) -> f(x) for these two is the correct call under the selection convention, and the suggested removal would spend evaluations on pairs that differ by <0.02 Sharpe.

result.corrected_fix:
The defect is real but both halves of the suggested fix need correcting.

1. "Gate it on hl == 0" is NOT implementable as the code stands, and this matters. Rules are matched against an expression string inside Guidance.canonical() (partura/steer.py:270) long before any reward runs, and the half-life is chosen per candidate inside steer.reward()/books.fit_halflives(). Pattern/Rule have no access to it. So the only sound options are removal or demotion.

2. Demote C4 out of `rewrite` — but note `weight` is not the semantic fix either, it is just the harmless one. The honest reading of the project's own evidence (B01_reverse_guidance.md:57: n=15, d median +0.00, 7% clearly better, 7% clearly worse) is that root cs_winsor is a coin flip, not something to sample less often. So either delete C4 outright, or set `action: weight, w: 1.0` purely to keep the note attached. Either form removes the three real harms at once, because all three flow from canonical(): the dedup_key collision (steer.py:283 -> idea_search.py:221), the silent seed rewrite (idea_search.py:244), and the inherited root verdict that makes `cs_winsor(cross_zscore(...))` carry B1's ban. A `dedup_key` action would NOT fix it — dedup_key is the harm, and `rewrite` is strictly stronger than `dedup_key` since it also feeds weight()/banned() and seed parsing.

3. Fix the rule's `why` while touching it: it quotes "ρ原式 0.99", which is the median (0.994); the min over the same 15 is 0.566, and 2 of 15 (F112 -0.99, F110 +0.31) move outside the declared 0.3 noise band with a train long_ann sign flip in both. State it as "usually harmless, occasionally decisive — a separate experiment, not a shorter spelling", and record that it is an exact identity only when the traded signal is unsmoothed (hl == 0, verified exactly), which R6's half-life grid almost never selects.

4. Do NOT touch IDEMPOTENT_OPS (partura/steer.py:171). Leave cs_winsor and cs_robust_z in. Measured book impact of collapsing f(f(x)) -> f(x) is +0.0175 and +0.0051 long_sharpe at hl=20 (0 at hl=0), against the project's own 0.3 noise band; removing them would spend evaluations on pairs that are the same experiment by the project's own standard. The reporter's "guard that only collapses when the rewrite is also applied to the smoothed panel" buys nothing at this magnitude.

5. Additional fix the finding does not mention: B01.yaml:156, idea I4_intraday_reversal_tail lists `cs_winsor(_)` in `grammar.convex`, which puts cs_winsor in IDEA_OPS and gives it an 8x sampling boost in the steer arm (idea_search.py:72-77, 196) while C4 strips it at the root. Whichever way C4 is resolved, these two lines must agree — otherwise the steer arm pays 8x the sampling for an operator whose root occurrences are all dedup-collapsed, which biases the episode's own headline number (distinct passers per 100 scored, steer vs control; the control arm does not run the dedup at all, idea_search.py:214-215).
